subject: Recap: Vector search / reranking discovery — index scale, targets, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@searchlytics.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — recap & next steps from today

Alex — thanks again for carving out 30 minutes today. Below is a short recap so we’re aligned and I can loop in the right folks for a technical deep dive / PoC. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: search relevance at scale — queries return stale or noisy results for newer content, customers complain about ranking.
- Current stack: Elasticsearch for filtering + a vendor-managed vector DB (SearchAVL / proprietary) for ANN; embedding generation is a mix of an internal OpenAI-based pipeline and on-device keyword heuristics.
- Scale: ~250M active vectors across multiple indices (articles, docs, product pages).
- Success criteria: top-K recall and business metric improvements (CTR) + 99th percentile retrieval latency < 25ms for candidate gen; overall reranked response under 120ms end-to-end for the low-latency tier. Cost target: keep incremental inference cost under $0.0008/query.
- Batch patterns: nightly re-ingest for new content (avg batch size ~150k vectors), real-time upserts for popular pages. Typical QPS: baseline 120qps with spikes to 650qps on peak events.

What we heard on reranking approach
- You currently generate 64-dim embeddings for candidate filtering and then run a cross-encoder style reranker on the top 200 candidates. Reranker currently hosted on CPU-limited infra; serving cost and latency are pain points.
- Warm cache hit-rate is moderate; prefix caching would help but you need consistent accuracy for tail queries.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Technical deep dive with Vivek (SE) to validate index shapes, embedding dims, candidate sizes, and reranker model. Goal: quantify shard/batch sizing, memory, and latency envelope. (Target: next Tue/Wed)
2) PoC scope: 1-week micro-benchmark on a representative index (10M vectors) to measure: retrieval latency at 1/10/100 qps, rerank latency on CPU vs GPU, end-to-end cost estimates.
3) Provide a short SOW + rollup pricing and an initial config for Dedicated capacity (if you need guaranteed throughput).
4) Share a minimal dataset / sample queries and your public query log (anonymized) so we can reproduce tail behavior.

Attachments: redwood-arch-sketch.png (lightweight diagram), initial-benchmarks.xlsx (template)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical session.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Thanks — recap & next steps from today

Marissa — thanks for the recap, very helpful and mostly on point. A couple clarifications: 
- Embedding dims: we actually have two pipelines; a 1536-dim (primary) and a 512-dim (fast path) for mobile. Majority of the index is 1536-dim (~210M).
- Candidate generation: we limit to 500 candidates today for broad recall, then rerank to top 10; reranker is a small transformer on a beefy CPU box (GCP n2-highmem family).
- Latency targets: the 120ms E2E you reference is for the premium low-latency SKU; for bulk queries we’re OK with 250–300ms. The $0.0008/query target is a hard business constraint.

I’ll get you an anonymized sample query log and a small export of the index metadata by COB Monday.

—Alex
Alex Turner
VP, Search Products | SearchLytics
alex.turner@searchlytics.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Thanks — recap & next steps from today

Alex / Marissa — quick technical notes ahead of the deep dive. High-level thoughts: 
- Index shape: 250M vectors at 1536 dims is non-trivial but common — need to confirm average vector byte-size (float16 vs quantized int8). If you can quantize to 8-bit per dimension we reduce memory 4x vs float32 which dramatically affects shard sizing.
- Vector DB: what vendor are you using for ANN? We’ve benchmarked Milvus, Faiss (flat/HNSW on GPU), and Weaviate; each has tradeoffs for write-heavy workloads and sharding. If your vendor is fully managed but opaque, we’ll want to validate nearest-neighbor recall vs RAM usage.
- Candidate count: dropping candidates from 500->200 often reduces reranker cost with minimal recall loss if embeddings + ANN are tuned. Worth testing in the PoC.
- Reranker options: 1) move reranker to batch-GPU (amortize cost) for peak windows, 2) use a distilled cross-encoder with half precision on GPU, or 3) hybrid approach — cheap bi-encoder score + small cross-encoder only on top 50.

For the PoC we should capture: QPS profiles (steady + spike), cold vs warm cache latency, memory util per node, and per-query cost number. Can you share:
- sample queries + anonymized user tokens (as Marissa requested)
- one week of QPS timeline (aggregated)
- current vector DB vendor and instance sizes

I’ll prepare a short matrix of options (latency vs cost vs accuracy) before the call.

-Vivek
